entries.title: DRAFT: Gaussian route selection changes the mean
entries.statement: Unreviewed campaign DRAFT; independent mathematical check pending. For v>0, rho in [-1,1], xi>0, two parallel edges with jointly centered Gaussian log fields X,Y of variance v and covariance rho*v have E[log min(exp(xi*X),exp(xi*Y))]=-xi*sqrt(v*(1-rho)/pi), although each fixed edge has centered log length.
assumptions: Joint Gaussian law with the stated covariance
entries.remaining_gap: Independent check pending. This is an elementary graph counterexample, not an LQG metric or a refutation of a dimension conjecture.

entries.title: DRAFT: Marginals do not determine crossing exponents
entries.statement: Unreviewed campaign DRAFT; independent mathematical check pending. Fix xi,kappa>0, epsilon_n=exp(-n) and m_n=ceil(exp(kappa*n)). On a graph of m_n parallel unit edges put D_n=min_i exp(xi*X_{n,i}) and let a_n be any median of D_n. If the fields within n are independent N(0,n), log(a_n)/log(epsilon_n) tends to xi*sqrt(2*kappa); if all fields are one common N(0,n), it tends to zero. Thus identical Gaussian edge marginals and D(X+c)=exp(xi*c)D(X) do not determine an optimized normalization exponent. No independence across n is needed. These growing graphs are not GFF or LQG models.
assumptions: Within each n the first model has independent Gaussian fields
The second model has one common Gaussian field
Geometry is the specified growing parallel-edge graph
Median crossing normalizer; no independence across n is needed
entries.remaining_gap: Independent check pending. Actual GFF covariance, planar crossing geometry and LQG locality are absent from this toy model; the full dimension remains unproved.

entries.title: DRAFT: Conditional two-route near-tie error bound
entries.statement: Unreviewed campaign DRAFT; independent mathematical check pending. Let X be a finite centered Gaussian vector with covariance C positive semidefinite, V=max_i C_ii, xi>0, and exactly two lengths l_p=sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), with nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors. Put f_p=log l_p, w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/l_p, Delta=f_1-f_2, R=(w_1-w_2)^T C(w_1-w_2), pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_{q=1}^2 exp(-beta f_q) and B_beta=pi_1*pi_2*R. Suppose nu(A)=E[R*1{Delta in A}] has density b on (-eta,eta), eta>0, and |b(t)-b(0)|<=L|t| there. For beta>0, |beta E B_beta-b(0)| <= 2 log(2)L/beta+(4 beta V+2 b(0))exp(-beta eta). No density assumption is needed outside this interval. For a cutoff family at scale T_n, divide this bound by T_n; a joint cutoff/temperature limit requires both resulting error terms to vanish and b_n(0)/T_n to have a determined limit. Those uniform hypotheses are not proved for LQG here.
assumptions: xi>0; two nonzero nonnegative finite coefficient vectors
C positive semidefinite; w are normalized exponential path weights
Local absolute continuity and stated Lipschitz bound for the weighted gap measure
entries.remaining_gap: Uniform cutoff-dependent gap-density bounds, convergence of b_n(0)/T_n, within-path occupation response and multi-route competitiveness remain unproved for LFPP.

entries.title: DRAFT: A third route suppresses a pair's switching term
entries.statement: Unreviewed campaign DRAFT; independent mathematical check pending. Let Z,U,V0 be independent N(0,1), xi>0, M>=0, and let three parallel edges have log lengths f1=xi(Z+U), f2=xi(Z-U), f3=-M+xi V0. Their Gaussian field covariance is diag(2,2,1), positive definite. For full soft weights pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_{q=1}^3 exp(-beta f_q), the covariance distance of pair 1,2 is R12=4 and lim_{beta->infinity} beta E[pi_1*pi_2*R12]=[2/(xi sqrt(2*pi))]*Phi(-M/(xi sqrt(2))), where Phi is the standard normal distribution function. The isolated two-route contribution is 2/(xi sqrt(2*pi)). At M=0 the full pair contribution is half; for large M its ratio tends to zero. Pair gap regularity alone does not justify substitution into a full-model switching sum: the pair must beat every other route at its tie. This finite example does not refute w516's qualified reduction or an LQG dimension formula.
assumptions: The full soft weights include all three routes
The third base length is exp(-M)>0
xi is fixed; beta tends to infinity
entries.remaining_gap: Finite model only. Refutes an unqualified isolated-pair replacement, not w516 L1-L5 or any LQG dimension formula.

relations.rationale: Both ends optimize Gaussian route lengths. O1 computes finite selection bias; O2 proves the same dependence issue can persist at normalization-exponent scale.
